chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from one of his companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them): Regarding a person performing Tamattu' who shaved his head,

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was forgetful or ignorant, there is no penalty upon him. And if he was a Mutamatti' at the beginning of the months of Hajj, there is no penalty upon him if he had been exempted for a month.'

key_terms.مُتَمِّتٍ: A pilgrim performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for shaving the head early during the Hajj of Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the penalty for premature shaving during the Hajj of Tamattu', distinguishing between unintentional errors (forgetfulness or ignorance) which incur no penalty, and intentional early shaving. It introduces a specific exemption for those who shave at the beginning of the Hajj months, provided they wait a full month to complete their Ihram obligations, reflecting the juristic principle of leniency in ritual errors. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of the Hajj and the specific compensations (kaffarah) required for breaking Ihram conditions.
